display: Arthur Robert Ashe Jr. was born in Richmond, Virginia, on July 10, 1943, to Mattie Cunningham Ashe and Arthur Robert Ashe Sr.; his mother died before he was seven.
On July 31, 1979, while teaching tennis to inner-city youth, Ashe had a heart attack, and he then underwent quadruple coronary artery bypass surgery in 1979.
When chest pain recurred, Ashe had a second bypass operation, a double bypass, in 1983, during which he received a blood transfusion.

In 1988 Ashe had difficulty moving his right hand and arm; a scan showed a mass in the left side of his brain, which surgeons removed, and the diagnosis was toxoplasmosis. Testing then showed that he had HIV and AIDS.
Ashe and his doctors concluded that he had almost certainly acquired HIV from a blood transfusion during his 1983 heart operation, before blood was tested for the virus.

Ashe kept his diagnosis private at first, telling only a few family members and friends. On April 8, 1992, after learning that USA Today planned to report it, he announced at a press conference that he had HIV.
Both of Ashe's parents had atherosclerotic heart disease at early ages. His mother died at 27 of complications from surgery, and his father had two heart attacks, at 55 and at 59.
Ashe died in New York City on February 6, 1993, aged 49, of AIDS-related pneumonia. His memoir, Days of Grace, was published after his death.
